external_source.archive_name: Seoul public bicycle hourly usage information, 2019 ZIP
external_source.license: Korea Open Government License Type 1 (KOGL Type 1): attribution

source_contract: Require an interpretable rental-hour timestamp and a rental-event or rental-count measure; aggregate all and only Seoul public bicycle rentals into exactly one nonnegative citywide count per local hour. Reject ambiguous units, duplicate aggregates, missing hours, gaps, invalid dates/counts, schema changes or incomplete 2019 coverage. Ignore demographic and station attributes. Do not repair or impute. Record raw archive and derived aggregate SHA-256 before scoring.
compatibility_gate: Confirm that the official source measures hourly citywide rentals, comparable in meaning to the UCI rental count. A different unit or unresolvable mismatch blocks scoring; do not rename a different target as validation.
forecast: At the end of source hour t, score the count in source hour t+24. Use only complete past counts and known target-hour calendar cycles; require 168 hours of prior 2019 history and a complete 2019 target hour.
model: Refit only the original fixed 2017-2018 training logistic pipeline and July 2018 sigmoid calibration. Use the original train-derived high-demand threshold and model settings. No 2019 fitting, threshold reset, feature changes, model selection or parameter tuning.
baselines: 2019 same target hour one week earlier
metrics: Brier score for calibrated probability and prevalence baseline
precision, recall and captures under one top-10%-of-all-eligible-2019-hours retrospective budget
reporting: Separate local-only external-source report. Compare descriptively with original 2018 result, disclose differing publisher/collection, city-scale shift, 2019 class support and publication latency. No operational, causal, statistical-significance or future-year generalization claim.
release: No raw source, derived row-level counts, or report in Git or public container. Keep the original benchmark and exploratory audit intact.

cross_check.rule: Obtain the four small official files covering 2019 daily rental counts, extract 365 dated counts with no ambiguity, and require every daily total to equal the sum of the 24 hourly aggregates. If a file is inaccessible, ambiguous or inconsistent, block scoring. Retain hashes and a summary only; no raw cross-check files in Git.
